{{short description|Italian mathematician and astronomer}}
[[File:Pappiani_-_Scienza_delle_grandezze,_1747_-_4256369.tif|thumb|Title page of the ''Scienza delle grandezze'' (1747)]]

'''Alberto Pappiani''' (1709–1790)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thesaurus.cerl.org/record/cnp00916048|title=Pappiani, Alberto|publisher=[[Consortium of European Research Libraries]]|language=it}}</ref> was an [[Italians|Italian]] [[mathematician]], [[astronomer]], and [[theologian]].

He was a [[Piarists|Piarist]] [[priest]] and [[teacher]] of [[philosophy]] and [[mathematics]] in the [[Florentine College]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Novelle letterarie pubblicate in Firenze|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0Y8EAAAAQAAJ&pg=PT817|volume=8|year=1747|location=Florence|page=817|language=it}}</ref>

In 1758, he became president of the [[Academy of Dogmatic Theologians]] in [[Florence]].<ref>{{Cite book|first=Antonella|last=Alimento|chapter=Le accademie ecclesiastiche: Roma, Napoli e Firenze|title=Naples, Rome, Florence: Une histoire comparée des milieux intellectuels italiens (XVII-XVIIIe siècles)|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uA0RCwAAQBAJ&pg=PA628|year=2013|location=Rome|publisher=École française de Rome|isbn=978-2-7283-1015-9|page=628}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|first=Michele|last=Maylender|title=Storia delle accademie d'Italia|volume=5|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=o9_QAAAAMAAJ&pg=PA303|year=1930|location=Bologna|publisher=L. Cappelli|page=303|language=it}}</ref>
